thread:
marta: Heads-up — I dug into rate limiting gaps for per-route limits. We need per-route shaping (chat/embeddings/rerank/streaming) + priority lanes/hysteresis so bursts don't kill streaming sessions.
kai: +1. High-level: chat = token-heavy, needs token rate + concurrency limits. embeddings = CPU/memory heavy, prefer qps limits. streaming = long-lived connections, prefer connection weight + token cap. rerank = small inputs but can be high-qps, treat as latency-sensitive.
zane: Where do we enforce? API gateway (fast), or runtime (accurate token counts)? Gateway can't see token counts pre-generation.
samir: We already have X-Token-Estimate header from router. Could use that for pre-checks in gateway. It's not perfect but helps avoid obvious bursts.
ashley: UI ask: console should show per-route burst window, current burst headroom per key/org and time-to-refill. Also add a "degraded" flag when fallbacks are active so customers can see impact.
marta: Example headers I'd like to standardize so callers can make smart backoff decisions:
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 300
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 27
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1672531200
X-Token-Burst-Remaining: 12000
```
kai: We need hysteresis: when we throttle, prefer shedding embeddings first, then rerank, then chat, and never interrupt established streaming sessions unless outage. That ordering aligns with revenue/latency impact.
zane: Also consider priority lanes for enterprise customers (reserved concurrency). That implies per-key and per-org budgets that can be borrowed during idle and reclaimed with cooldown.
samir: On enforcement flow: gateway does quick checks using estimated tokens and qps; runtime validates final token usage and refunds/credits. If runtime rejects for overage, gateway should attempt fallback model or enqueue a short retry.
ashley: Telemetry requirements: record route, model, tokens_est, tokens_actual, enforcement_point (gateway/runtime), decision, and reason. Expose these filters in the console to slice by key/org/route.
marta: UX for rollouts: when we lower burst cap for a route, show an "expected error spike" projection and allow a canary toggle: route X% through new policy for 24h. Add immediate rollback button + alert if error rate > threshold.
kai: Edge case: streaming reconnect storms when we abruptly close streams. Need a graceful drain: mark route as "no-new-streams" and allow existing sessions to finish under soft limit, plus delayed reclaim.
zane: Implementation sketch: maintain per-key token-bucket in Redis with two counters: burst_allowance and refill_rate. Gateway atomically decrements burst_allowance via Lua script; runtime reconciles final token usage asynchronously and updates refund ledger.
samir: Watch out for clock skew and race conditions. Add local in-memory caches with very short TTL to reduce Redis QPS and avoid thundering herd. Use idempotency keys for refund writes.
ashley: I'll mock console visuals and sample telemetry queries (Grafana) and link to RFC once ready.
marta: Who owns gateway change?
kai: Kai+Zane can pair on gateway L4/L7 changes.
samir: I own runtime reconciliation and refund flow.
ashley: I'll own console telemetry + UI. I'll also add a "burst headroom" widget for per-key.
marta: I'll open an RFC with the full design and cost estimates. Tagging infra for Redis capacity.
quota-bot: Scheduled: created RFC #482 "route-priority-burst-hysteresis". Review requested in 48h.
marta: Thanks — let's sync Thurs 10am. :thumbsup:
